title: hypothesis: Truncated BPTT with 15-20-trial windows under closed-loop reward is numerically stable with the spec's optimizer settings
description:
Gap G5 from astabot-pavi-q5k: published closed-loop work (Song 2016, Ger & Barak 2025) uses policy-gradient RL with shorter horizons; the spec's BCE-on-z combined with window-based detachment over multi-trial blocks has no direct published precedent.

Statement: With Adam at lr=1e-3 (Stages 0-3) / lr=1e-4 (Stage 4), gradient clipping at max-norm 1.0, the spec's L2 firing-rate and weight regularizers, and a truncated BPTT window of W=15-20 trials, training is numerically stable: gradient norms remain bounded, training loss does not exhibit divergent oscillations across windows, and stage advancement is monotone in mean d' (no >50% regression rate across seeds within a stage).

Why: The combination of closed-loop reward (network output gates its own future inputs), long temporal horizons (15-20 trials = 1875-2500 timesteps), and a sigmoid scalar readout has known potential for instability that the literature has not characterized at this scale.

Falsifiable prediction: Across 20+ training runs at the spec's settings, log per-window gradient norms, per-window training loss, and per-evaluation-checkpoint d's. Hypothesis predicts (a) per-window gradient norms post-clipping concentrated around 1.0 with no runaway, (b) training loss decreases or is flat across consecutive windows in steady-state for >= 90% of windows, (c) <= 10% of seeds regress from Stage 1+ to Stage 0 during training.

Inputs: scope astabot-pavi-x8g; literature_review astabot-pavi-q5k.

title: hypothesis: All 5 instruction trials per block contribute to context-belief update; d' recovery requires the full preamble
description:
Gap G4 from astabot-pavi-q5k: no prior model studies trial-by-trial dynamics of context-belief update with the 5-trial instruction preamble; whether all 5 are necessary is unique-to-this-project measurement (validation check #3 in the spec).

Statement: In a Stage-4-passing RNN, the post-switch d'_intra and d'_inter at the first post-instruction trial increases monotonically with the number of instruction trials actually presented (1, 2, 3, 4, 5), and falls below Stage-4 criteria (d' > 1.5 on 4/6 blocks) when fewer than 5 instruction trials are used.

Why: The instruction trials are the only signal disambiguating the new block rule; reducing their count must reduce the strength of the context-belief update, but the literature does not specify how this reduction scales.

Falsifiable prediction: Replay evaluation sessions on a trained Stage-4 RNN with k=1,2,3,4,5 instruction trials at each block boundary. Plot d'_intra and d'_inter on the 6 post-instruction-segment blocks as a function of k. Hypothesis predicts strict monotonic increase in mean d' and Stage-4 criterion satisfied only at k=5 (or possibly k=4).

Inputs: scope astabot-pavi-x8g; literature_review astabot-pavi-q5k.

title: hypothesis: Stage-4 ensemble solutions converge on a single latent-circuit motif (modality-selective context populations + gated readout)
description:
Gap G3 from astabot-pavi-q5k: Dubreuil 2022 predicts multi-population low-rank structure for flexible context-dependent tasks; whether unconstrained seeds converge on one mechanism or many is an open empirical question.

Statement: Across N >= 20 seeds that pass Stage 4, the trained RNNs share a single dominant latent-circuit motif: two context-selective sub-populations whose activity gates the modality-specific sensory-to-readout pathway via mutual inhibition, qualitatively matching the Langdon & Engel 2025 / Hajnal 2024 mechanism.

Why: Dubreuil 2022 and Driscoll 2024 argue that low-rank dynamical motifs are the natural attractor of training under inductive-bias constraints; the spec's non-negative W_in and ReLU activations likely funnel all seeds into the same motif class.

Falsifiable prediction: Cluster the per-seed latent-circuit fits or per-seed PCA loadings across N >= 20 seeds; cluster occupancy is concentrated (>= 80% of seeds in one cluster) and inter-cluster mechanism descriptions overlap on the modality-selective context population + gated readout pattern.

Inputs: scope astabot-pavi-x8g; literature_review astabot-pavi-q5k.

title: hypothesis: 5-stage curriculum alone insufficient for stable context substrate; line-attractor regularization or context-attractor init required
description:
Gap G2 from astabot-pavi-q5k: project v9-v11 logs and background_knowledge.txt show plain curriculum fails to bridge cross-block context (d'_inter ~= 0); literature (Koppe 2019, Khajehabdollahi 2023) suggests explicit attractor regularizer or slow-timescale init is needed.

Statement: Without an explicit line-attractor regularizer on the Jacobian (Koppe 2019) or a context-attractor weight initialization (the rank-1 W_rec update documented in background_knowledge.txt), the spec's 5-stage curriculum will not produce d'_inter > 1.5 across 4/6 blocks in any of N>=10 seeds within the stage-advancement budget.

Why: Effective recurrent eigenvalue under alpha=0.2 dynamics decays context signal to <1% within one trial; without a structural fix to the recurrence, BPTT gradients on Block-1 vs Block-2 context cancel and the network converges to a context-invariant strategy.

Falsifiable prediction: Pair of training runs at matched seeds (N>=10), one with context-attractor init / line-attractor regularizer, one without. Without the fix: d'_inter < 1.5 on all seeds. With the fix: at least one seed reaches Stage 4.

Inputs: scope astabot-pavi-x8g; literature_review astabot-pavi-q5k.

title: hypothesis: 5-stage curriculum reaches Stage 4 on dynamic routing without explicit context channel
description:
Gap G1 from astabot-pavi-q5k literature review: no published RNN combines the spec's task definition, no-context-channel architecture, and closed-loop reward delivery. Headline empirical claim of Phase 1.

Statement: An RNN with N=200 ReLU units, tau=100 ms, sigma_rec=0.15, non-negative W_in, scalar sigmoid readout, no explicit context input channel, and closed-loop late_autoreward instruction-trial semantics, trained via the spec's 5-stage curriculum, will satisfy Stage 4 advancement criteria (d'_intra > 1.5 AND d'_inter > 1.5 on at least 4/6 blocks across at least 5 consecutive evaluation sessions).

Why: The literature shows context-dependent RNNs trained with explicit cues (Mante 2013) or meta-RL belief states (Wang 2018) can reach criterion; whether the spec's specific combination of architecture + closed-loop reward + curriculum closes the gap is the project's headline question.

Falsifiable prediction: Across 50 seeds, at least one seed reaches Stage 4 and passes validation checks #1-#6 (hits >= 0.8, FAs <= 0.2, near-zero catch-trial licks, 6-10 PCs > 90% variance).

Inputs: scope astabot-pavi-x8g; literature_review astabot-pavi-q5k.

title: literature_review: Survey prior work on context-inferring RNNs and dynamic routing
close_reason: literature_review complete; summary at literature_review.md; 22 citations across 5 themes; 5 gaps motivating downstream hypotheses

gaps: G1: No published RNN combines (a) the dynamic-routing task at the spec's trial-level resolution, (b) no explicit context channel, and (c) closed-loop reward delivery gated by the network's own sigmoid output. Hajnal 2024, Orlandi 2021, and Mante 2013 each relax at least one of these constraints. Phase 1 is a genuinely new demonstration.

G2: The spec's 5-stage curriculum is not known to produce a stable context attractor. The project's own v9-v11 logs and the analysis in `background_knowledge.txt` show plain curriculum fails to bridge cross-block context, and the literature (Koppe 2019, Khajehabdollahi 2023) supports the hypothesis that an explicit Jacobian / line-attractor regularizer or a slow-timescale init is needed. Worth testing as the first downstream hypothesis.

G3: Solution diversity across the 50-seed ensemble is empirically untested at this combination of task and architecture. Dubreuil 2022 predicts multi-population low-rank structure should emerge; whether 50 unconstrained seeds produce one mechanism with weight noise or many qualitatively different mechanisms is open and measurable here.

G4: The trial-by-trial dynamics of context-belief update within the 5-instruction-trial preamble are not predicted by any prior model — every closely-related architecture either has an explicit context cue or a teacher-forced reward stream. Whether all 5 instruction trials are necessary, and how fast d' recovers after a block switch, is unique-to-this-project measurement (validation check #3).

G5: Stability of truncated BPTT through 15-20-trial windows under closed-loop reward feedback is unknown a priori. Published closed-loop work (Song 2016, Ger & Barak 2025) uses policy-gradient REINFORCE with shorter horizons; the spec's BCE-on-z combined with window-based detachment over multi-trial blocks has no direct published precedent and may exhibit undocumented instability modes.

citations.title: Context-dependent computation by recurrent dynamics in prefrontal cortex
citations.relevance: Founding paper of the RNN-modeling-of-context-dependent-decision-making framework; trained RNN reproduces macaque PFC dynamics via a line-attractor mechanism. The Phase 2 latent-circuit fit will target the same kind of mechanism.

citations.title: Latent circuit inference from heterogeneous neural responses during cognitive tasks
citations.relevance: The latent-circuit framework the spec's Phase 2 explicitly uses. Recovers a context-suppression mechanism from a context-dependent-task RNN — the exact prediction for what Phase 1 should find.

citations.title: Linking Connectivity, Dynamics, and Computations in Low-Rank Recurrent Neural Networks
citations.relevance: Theoretical foundation of low-rank RNN theory; dimensionality of dynamics equals rank of structured connectivity. Sets expectations for the 6-10 PCs > 90% variance validation check.

citations.title: The role of population structure in computations through neural dynamics
citations.relevance: Shows that flexible context-dependent computation requires multi-population low-rank structure with gain modulations — the structural prediction for what Phase 1's RNN should develop.

citations.title: Shaping Dynamics With Multiple Populations in Low-Rank Recurrent Networks
citations.relevance: Companion theoretical paper to Dubreuil 2022; rank-R, P-population low-rank RNN can approximate any R-dim dynamical system.

citations.title: Prefrontal cortex as a meta-reinforcement learning system
citations.relevance: Closest conceptual ancestor: RNN with (obs, reward, action) inputs and no explicit task cue infers the current task from its recurrent state. Phase 1 inherits this architecture for a 2-MDP family.

citations.title: RL²: Fast Reinforcement Learning via Slow Reinforcement Learning
citations.relevance: ML-side precursor to Wang 2018; recurrent net's activations store the state of a fast inner-loop RL algorithm. The 7-channel input convention with reward and own-lick is structurally RL².

citations.title: Shifts in attention drive context-dependent subspace encoding in anterior cingulate cortex in mice during decision making
citations.relevance: Closest published behavioral analogue of the dynamic-routing task: mice attend to rewarded modality among identical visual+auditory stimuli with no external cue; modeled with an RNN that develops context-gated mutual inhibition between modality ensembles.

citations.title: Distributed context-dependent choice information in mouse posterior cortex
citations.relevance: Mouse visual decision task with RNN modeling; validates that mouse-scale context-dependent tasks are captured by trained RNNs and yield low-dimensional decision subspaces.

citations.title: Thalamic control of sensory selection in divided attention
citations.relevance: Classic cued cross-modal attention task in mice; sets the experimental benchmark for sensory-selection mechanisms and clarifies that the dynamic-routing task is the harder, uncued analogue.

citations.title: Opening the Black Box: Low-Dimensional Dynamics in High-Dimensional Recurrent Neural Networks
citations.relevance: Slow-point methodology for reverse-engineering trained RNNs — the analytical lineage validation checks #4 and #5 depend on.

citations.title: FixedPointFinder: A Tensorflow toolbox for identifying and characterizing fixed points in recurrent neural networks
citations.relevance: Reusable implementation of fixed-/slow-point finding; an architectural template for the post-training analysis code.

citations.title: Inferring Dynamical Systems with Long-Range Dependencies through Line Attractor Regularization
citations.relevance: Direct published precedent for line-attractor regularization to maintain a slow context variable — addresses the spec's vanishing-context-gradient pitfall and the project's documented v9-v11 failure mode.

citations.title: Task representations in neural networks trained to perform many cognitive tasks
citations.relevance: Curriculum + cluster analysis template for RNNs on cognitive tasks; the spec's mixed-selectivity validation check (#4) descends from this analysis.

citations.title: Flexible multitask computation in recurrent networks utilizes shared dynamical motifs
citations.relevance: Catalogs dynamical motifs (line attractors, ring attractors, decision boundaries) that ReLU RNNs reuse, and shows they are implemented by clustered sub-populations. The latent-circuit prediction for Phase 1 is one such motif.

citations.title: Emergent mechanisms for long timescales depend on training curriculum and affect performance in memory tasks
citations.relevance: Curriculum order determines whether trained RNNs use line attractors or other mechanisms for long timescales — directly relevant to whether the spec's 5-stage curriculum alone suffices for the dynamic-routing context substrate.

citations.title: Understanding and Controlling Memory in Recurrent Neural Networks
citations.relevance: Mechanistic analysis of memory horizon in RNNs and regularizers that control it — useful for diagnosing the project's vanishing-context-gradient problem.

citations.title: Reward-based training of recurrent neural networks for cognitive and value-based tasks
citations.relevance: Canonical demonstration of closed-loop reward-driven RNN training on cognitive tasks via REINFORCE — the structural precedent for Phase 1's training paradigm.

citations.title: Learning Dynamics of RNNs in Closed-Loop Environments
citations.relevance: Recent systematic analysis of how training dynamics differ when network output gates its own input distribution — directly relevant for diagnosing Stage 0-2 instability modes.

citations.title: From fixed points to chaos: three models of delayed discrimination
citations.relevance: Shows that three different attractor structures (fixed points, line attractor, chaotic transient) can implement the same delay computation; sets expectations for the diversity of solutions the spec's curriculum may select.

citations.title: PsychRNN: An Accessible and Flexible Python Package for Training Recurrent Neural Network Models on Cognitive Tasks
citations.relevance: Reference implementation of supervised RNN training on cognitive tasks; an explicit comparator for the project's training code architecture.

citations.title: Emergence of hybrid computational dynamics through reinforcement learning
citations.relevance: Recent example showing that RL-trained RNNs spontaneously develop hybrid attractor + transient dynamics — informs expectations for the kind of solution structure Phase 1 may find.

key_findings: Mante, Sussillo, Shenoy & Newsome (2013, Nature) established the framework the project sits in: macaque PFC context-dependent integration is reproduced by a trained continuous-time RNN whose mechanism is a line attractor that selects task-relevant inputs and integrates them to choice.

Langdon & Engel (2025, Nature Neuroscience) is the latent-circuit framework that the spec's Phase 2 will plug Phase 1 into. Applied to RNNs trained on a context-dependent task, it recovers a suppression mechanism in which contextual representations inhibit irrelevant sensory pathways — directly predicting the kind of mechanism the spec expects to find post-training.

Low-rank RNN theory (Mastrogiuseppe & Ostojic 2017 Neuron; Beirán et al. 2020 Neural Comp; Dubreuil et al. 2022 Nat Neurosci) shows that context-dependent / flexible tasks require multi-population structure with gain-modulated low-rank connectivity — independent theoretical support for the latent-circuit hypothesis (Dubreuil 2022 in particular: a single global population cannot implement flexible input-output mappings).

Wang et al. (2018, Nature Neuroscience) 'Prefrontal cortex as meta-RL' and Duan et al. (2016, arXiv) 'RL²' show that an RNN whose inputs include reward and previous action can encode an implicit belief about the current task in its recurrent state — the architectural paradigm Phase 1 inherits, restricted to a 2-MDP family (vis1-rewarded vs aud1-rewarded blocks).

Hajnal et al. (2024, Nat Comm) is the closest published behavioral analogue of the dynamic-routing task: head-fixed mice attend to the rewarded modality among identical visual+auditory stimuli with no external context cue, and the authors model ACC with an RNN that develops context-gated mutual inhibition between modality-selective ensembles — essentially the latent-circuit mechanism the spec predicts.

Slow-point / fixed-point analysis tools (Sussillo & Barak 2013 Neural Comp; Golub & Sussillo 2018 JOSS FixedPointFinder) and the dynamical-motif catalog (Driscoll, Shenoy & Sussillo 2024 Nat Neurosci) provide off-the-shelf machinery for validation checks #4 and #5 in the spec.

Line-attractor regularization (Koppe, Beutelspacher & Durstewitz 2019, arXiv) and curriculum-dependent emergence of long timescales (Khajehabdollahi et al. 2023, ICLR) directly address the spec's largest known training risk — the vanishing-context-gradient problem documented in `background_knowledge.txt`. Plain curriculum training without an explicit attractor regularizer may not produce a stable context substrate.

Closed-loop reward-driven RNN training is comparatively under-studied. Song, Yang & Wang (2016, eLife) is the canonical demonstration and Ger & Barak (2025, arXiv) is the most recent systematic analysis. The spec's late_autoreward + sigmoid-threshold-gated reward delivery has no direct published analogue — the project will be at the leading edge of this sub-literature.

title: definitions: Specify task protocol, RNN architecture, and training setup

terms.name: Dynamic routing task
terms.rationale: Pin down the task at the level the RNN sees it, separately from the experimental rig. This is the unit against which all advancement criteria and validation checks are measured.
terms.operational_definition: A block-based, context-dependent sensory detection task in which the network sees one of five trial conditions (vis1, vis2, aud1, aud2, or catch) and must lick if and only if the presented stimulus is the currently-rewarded target. The currently-rewarded target alternates between vis1 and aud1 across 6 blocks per session, is never explicitly cued, and must be inferred online from reward/own-lick feedback.

terms.name: Block
terms.rationale: The block is the unit at which the latent context belief must change. Many advancement criteria and validation checks are computed per-block, so a precise definition removes ambiguity downstream.
terms.operational_definition: A contiguous segment of one session containing exactly one rewarded target (vis1 OR aud1). A block consists of (a) 5 instruction trials presenting the newly-rewarded target with late_autoreward semantics, followed by (b) ~85 regular trials in which all four stimuli plus catch trials (p=0.1) are presented in 20-trial shuffled sub-blocks. A session contains 6 blocks with the rewarded target alternating each block; the first-block rewarded target is counterbalanced across training sessions.

terms.name: Instruction trial (late_autoreward semantics)
terms.rationale: Instruction trials are the primary signal that the block rule has changed; downstream hypotheses about context-update speed and circuit structure depend on this exact behavior. The spec also notes the alternative early_autoreward variant from the experiment — we explicitly use late_autoreward.
terms.operational_definition: The first 5 trials of every block in Stages 3 and 4. Each presents the newly-rewarded target stimulus. A non-contingent reward is scheduled for the end of the response window, but if the network licks (z > 0.5) anywhere within the response window the scheduled reward is cancelled and a contingent reward is delivered immediately at the lick timestep. The own-lick channel still fires on any lick.

terms.name: Repeat cues
terms.rationale: mission.md uses the phrase 'repeat cues' for what the spec calls 'instruction trials'. Bind the mission's vocabulary to the spec's vocabulary once so downstream tasks don't accidentally diverge.
terms.operational_definition: The mission's term for the sequence of 5 consecutive instruction trials at the start of each block, all presenting the newly-rewarded target. Operationally identical to 'instruction trials' (see above); the term emphasizes their role as the repeated, contingency-disambiguating signal that lets the network infer the new block rule without an explicit context channel.

terms.name: Catch trial
terms.rationale: Catch trials are the leakage test in validation check #6. The absence of input must itself be the signal — there is no dedicated catch channel.
terms.operational_definition: A trial with no stimulus on any of u[0]–u[3] for the entire stimulus window; u[4]–u[6] follow their usual logic (no reward will fire because no rewarded target is present). Presented with probability 0.1 within each shuffled 20-trial sub-block after the 5 instruction trials. The network should produce z < 0.5 throughout the response window; any lick on a catch trial counts as a false alarm.

terms.name: Trial timeline
terms.rationale: Exact step counts determine loss masking, when the own-lick/reward channels can fire, and how BPTT windows align. Any off-by-one here propagates everywhere.
terms.operational_definition: Each trial is exactly 125 timesteps at dt = 20 ms (2.5 s total): a 75-step quiescent period (1.5 s, all sensory channels zero, no loss computed), a 25-step stimulus-on window (0.5 s, stimulus channel = 1.0 if non-catch), and a 45-step response window from step 80 to step 124 (0.1–1.0 s after stimulus onset, inclusive of the last 0.4 s of stimulus-on plus 0.5 s of stimulus-off). u[6] (trial phase) is 1.0 only during the response window. Trials are concatenated directly within a block — the next trial's quiescent period begins at the timestep immediately after the previous trial's response window closes. No ITI, no post-response interval.

terms.name: Closed-loop reward delivery
terms.rationale: This is the closed-loop coupling that makes the task self-supervised — it's what forces the network to use feedback. Several spec pitfalls (#3) hinge on getting the timing of these pulses exactly right; pin it down once.
terms.operational_definition: During training (and any evaluation that uses regular trials), reward and own-lick channels are driven by the network's own behavior, not pre-scripted. At each response-window timestep, threshold z at 0.5. On the first timestep where z > 0.5: (a) fire u[5] (own lick) at 1.0 for 2 timesteps (40 ms); (b) if the current stimulus is the currently-rewarded target, also fire u[4] (reward) at 1.0 for those same 2 timesteps. Subsequent lick crossings within the same response window do not re-fire either channel. Instruction trials override the reward rule per their late_autoreward definition.

terms.name: Context belief
terms.rationale: Multiple downstream success criteria (block-transition curves, context-inference speed) reference context belief; without a precise behavioral definition we can't measure it.
terms.operational_definition: A property of the recurrent hidden state y(t), not a labeled channel. Defined operationally as: the network has the correct context belief at time t if, given a hypothetical immediate stimulus-onset at t+1, its z output during the resulting response window would match the target dictated by the currently-rewarded target of the block in which t falls. There is no input channel, no auxiliary loss, and no explicit decoder for context — it is implicit in the dynamics of y.

terms.name: Hit rate / False-alarm rate (per stimulus, per block type)
terms.rationale: Validation checks #1 and #6 depend on this; without a fixed convention (post-instruction vs. all trials; any-timestep crossing vs. terminal z) the numbers won't be comparable across runs.
terms.operational_definition: On an evaluation session of 6 blocks: for each stimulus s ∈ {vis1, vis2, aud1, aud2, catch} and each block type b ∈ {vis1-rewarded, aud1-rewarded}, compute the fraction of post-instruction (i.e. non-instruction) trials with stimulus s in b-typed blocks for which any z(t) > 0.5 occurred during the response window. P(lick|s_rewarded, b) is the hit rate; P(lick|s_unrewarded, b) is the false-alarm rate for that stimulus.

terms.name: d'_intra and d'_inter
terms.rationale: Stage-3 and Stage-4 advancement gates are stated in terms of these; downstream hypothesis and analysis tasks need a single agreed formula.
terms.operational_definition: Per-block, signal-detection-theoretic discriminability indices, computed on post-instruction trials only. For a vis1-rewarded block: d'_intra = Z(P(lick|vis1)) − Z(P(lick|vis2)), and d'_inter = Z(P(lick|vis1)) − Z(P(lick|aud1)), where Z is the inverse standard-normal CDF. For an aud1-rewarded block the rewarded target is aud1, the same-modality non-target is aud2, and the cross-modality target is vis1. Rates equal to 0 or 1 are clipped to (1/(2N), 1 − 1/(2N)) for a block of N trials before applying Z, to keep d' finite.

terms.name: Stage advancement criterion
terms.rationale: The curriculum is the spine of training; conflating 'evaluation checkpoint' with 'evaluation session' or shifting the 4-of-6 threshold would silently change results.
terms.operational_definition: Stages 1–2: at the most recent two consecutive evaluation checkpoints (every 100 training steps, 5 sessions per checkpoint, no noise, no gradient), d' > 1.5 on the relevant discrimination. Stage 3: at the most recent two consecutive evaluation sessions, both d'_intra > 1.5 AND d'_inter > 1.5 hold on at least 4 of the 6 blocks per session. Stage 4: 5 consecutive evaluation sessions with the same gate as Stage 3 plus no upward drift in the regularized loss. Failure to meet the gate keeps the network in the current stage; meeting it advances. Stage 0 advances by a fixed step count (e.g., 500 steps) with no performance gate.

terms.name: Stage regression criterion
terms.rationale: Without this, a network can get stuck in extinction. Downstream analyses of training dynamics need to know when a seed regressed.
terms.operational_definition: Per spec, in Stages 1–3: if hits < 10 across a full evaluation session (or evaluation checkpoint at Stage-1/2 granularity) for 2 consecutive checkpoints, revert the network to Stage 0 and restart from that point. No regression in Stage 0 or Stage 4.

terms.name: Truncated BPTT window
terms.rationale: This is the only mechanism by which the network can learn from reward feedback while still fitting in GPU memory. Several spec pitfalls (#2, #8) point at it.
terms.operational_definition: During Stages 3–4 (and any other multi-trial stage), the forward pass carries y across all trials in a block without reset, but autograd's computation graph is detached at the boundary of each window of W consecutive trials (W = 15–20 trials, configurable). Gradient updates are applied at the end of each window. The hidden state itself is not reset across windows — only its gradient history is. Stages 0–2 use single-trial windows (W = 1) since there is no cross-trial context to learn.

terms.name: Ensemble seed
terms.rationale: Validation checks and any future Phase-2 work depend on having multiple independent solutions. Treat the ensemble size as a budget knob, not a hidden default.
terms.operational_definition: An independent training run with its own random seed controlling weight init, noise streams, trial-order sampling, and stage-transition timing. The reference target is 50 seeds; the project may run a smaller ensemble if compute is constrained, but the reduction MUST be documented (number of seeds, why, and which downstream criteria are affected).

terms.name: Validation check (post-training)
terms.rationale: The spec lists six checks but does not name them collectively. Fixing the name and the numeric thresholds in one place keeps downstream synthesis and any report consistent.
terms.operational_definition: The six post-training analyses enumerated in the spec, each producing a concrete metric on held-out evaluation sessions of the final Stage-4 network: (1) hit/FA rates by block type, (2) block-transition lick curves aligned to block boundaries, (3) context-inference speed (trial index at which d' first exceeds 1.0 after a block switch), (4) heterogeneous mixed selectivity from per-unit response visualizations, (5) PCA on trial-averaged responses, (6) catch-trial leakage. A 'passing' RNN must satisfy: hits ≥ ~0.8, FAs ≤ ~0.2 averaged over equilibrated post-instruction trials, near-zero P(lick|catch), and ~6–10 PCs explaining > 90% of task-related variance. These are the only checks in scope for this project.

terms.name: Latent_circuit conda environment
terms.rationale: mission.md singles this out explicitly; pinning it in the definitions prevents drift to ad-hoc venvs.
terms.operational_definition: The conda environment named 'latent_circuit' as specified in mission.md (and defined in environment.yml at the repo root). All Python entry points (training, evaluation, analysis) are run inside this environment; the project does not introduce a second environment, requirements.txt, or pip-only install path.

title: scope: Define boundaries of RNN+dynamic-routing implementation

output.question: Can a recurrent neural network with no explicit context input learn to perform the dynamic routing task by inferring the current block rule from the conjunction of reward and own-lick feedback delivered during each trial's response window, and reach the spec's Stage 4 performance criteria (intra- and inter-modal d' > 1.5 on at least 4/6 blocks across consecutive evaluation sessions)?
boundaries: IN SCOPE: Implementation of Phase 1 of latent_circuit_dynamic_routing_spec.md — the ground-truth RNN that performs the dynamic routing task end-to-end.

IN SCOPE: The dynamic routing task itself — trial generation, 6-block sessions, 5-instruction-trial preambles, catch trials at p=0.1, late_autoreward instruction semantics, and the 125-step trial timeline (quiescent 75 + stim/response 50) at dt=20 ms, matching experiment_task_details/EXPERIMENT.md as closely as possible.

IN SCOPE: The 7-channel input convention (vis1, vis2, aud1, aud2, reward, own-lick, trial-phase) with NO explicit context channel; context must be inferred from the reward/own-lick feedback streams plus the repeated rewarded-target cues during the 5 instruction trials.

IN SCOPE: The DynamicRoutingRNN architecture as specified (N=200 ReLU units, tau=100 ms, alpha=0.2, sigma_rec=0.15, non-negative W_in, scalar sigmoid readout) with closed-loop reward/lick feedback during training.

IN SCOPE: The 5-stage curriculum (Stage 0 auto-rewards → Stage 1 visual discrimination → Stage 2 auditory discrimination → Stage 3 block switching with timeout → Stage 4 final fine-tune), including stage advancement gates based on d', windowed BPTT over 15–20 trials, and the regularization, optimizer, and gradient-clipping hyperparameters listed in the spec.

IN SCOPE: Post-training validation checks #1–#6 from the spec (hit/FA rates by block type, block-transition dynamics, context-inference speed, single-unit mixed selectivity, PCA variance explained, catch-trial leakage), used to confirm the trained RNN solves the task as intended.
IN SCOPE: A small ensemble of trained RNNs (~50 random seeds per the spec, reducible if compute-bound) so that downstream phases — if pursued later — could fit latent circuits to them.
IN SCOPE: Use of the existing 'latent_circuit' conda environment and PyTorch as the implementation framework.
OUT OF SCOPE: Phase 2 of the spec — fitting LatentCircuit models (the 9-node low-dimensional circuit, Stiefel-manifold Q optimization, neural+behavioral fitting loss) to the trained RNNs.

OUT OF SCOPE: Phase 3 of the spec — connectivity-conjugation validation, activity-projection analyses, rank-one perturbation experiments, decoder comparisons, block-transition latent dynamics, and ensemble solution-space PCA.
OUT OF SCOPE: Reproducing the Langdon & Engel (2025, Nature Neuroscience) Mante-task results or comparing to that reference implementation beyond reusing its Net/LatentNet patterns where convenient.
OUT OF SCOPE: Fitting against real mouse behavioral or electrophysiology data — the project trains and evaluates only against the task definition, not against recorded subject data.

OUT OF SCOPE: Architectural variants beyond the spec — e.g., Dale's-law-constrained W_rec (listed as optional in the spec), LSTMs/GRUs/Transformers, attention modules, alternative noise models, or alternative time constants/unit counts. Stick to the single architecture specified.
OUT OF SCOPE: Changes to the task itself — e.g., adding a stimulus-coherence gradient, varying block lengths beyond the spec, removing instruction trials, or adding an explicit context channel.
OUT OF SCOPE: Production-grade engineering — distributed training infrastructure, hyperparameter sweeps beyond what is needed to satisfy advancement criteria, deployment, model serving, or web UIs.
success_criteria: A DynamicRoutingRNN implementation exists in models/ matching the spec's architecture, hyperparameters, and weight constraints (non-negative W_in; ReLU; tau=100 ms; dt=20 ms; sigma_rec=0.15; N=200).

A task pipeline exists in tasks/ that generates 6-block sessions with the correct trial timeline, 5 instruction trials per block with late_autoreward semantics, catch trials at p=0.1, and shuffled stimulus sampling in 20-trial sub-blocks after instruction trials.

Reward delivery is closed-loop during training: u[4] (reward) and u[5] (own-lick) fire as 40-ms pulses driven by the network's own z(t) crossings of 0.5 within the response window, with reward gated by 'is this the currently rewarded target?'. No explicit context channel is provided to the network.

A 5-stage curriculum runs end-to-end with the spec's advancement gates (d' > 1.5 over 2 consecutive evaluation checkpoints in Stages 1–3; both d'_intra and d'_inter > 1.5 on 4-of-6 blocks across 2 consecutive sessions in Stage 3; convergence over 5 consecutive sessions in Stage 4) and the spec's regression criterion (revert to Stage 0 on persistent <10 hits).

Training uses truncated BPTT with a 15–20-trial window, Adam with lr=1e-3 (Stages 0–3) / 1e-4 (Stage 4), gradient clipping at max-norm 1.0, the spec's L2 firing-rate and weight regularizers, and 50-seed ensemble (reducible if necessary, with the reduction documented).

Post-training, the validation checks #1–#6 from the spec are computed and reported: hits ~0.8+ and FAs ~0.2 or less on a held-out evaluation, near-zero lick probability on catch trials, ~6–10 PCs covering >90% of task-related variance, and a measurable per-block context-update timescale (block-aligned P(lick|rewarded target) curves) demonstrating that the network is in fact using reward/lick feedback to switch contexts.

Training-time logs record per-evaluation-checkpoint metrics (stage, training step, d's, hit/FA rates, advancement decisions) so that learning dynamics and curriculum transitions can be inspected post hoc.
All code runs reproducibly within the 'latent_circuit' conda environment specified in mission.md.
